_comment: Which of condor's agents bench sizes a model for, and which it does not.
condor separates agents from strategies by storage, not by a field: a strategy is
created *under* an agent (create_strategy(slug, ...) writes into strategy.dir) and
inherits that agent's identity. Everything in condor's agents/ directory is an
agent by that definition. But the roster has grown to include entries that are
really specialisations of another agent -- an XRPL market maker is a market maker
pointed at one connector -- and giving each its own routing domain would multiply
recommendations every time a user ships one, on evidence that is the base
specialist's evidence under a different name.
condor does not encode this distinction (created_by does not correlate: two
experts carry a user id, two carry 0, one carries none), so bench records it here.
role: expert   -> gets a routing domain and a CONDOR_CONFIG_KEYS entry
role: strategy -> no routing domain; evidence comes from Layer 2 tool competence
Every agent condor ships must appear here. An unclassified agent fails
on purpose: the decision should be made deliberately once, not defaulted
silently in either direction. If condor ever adds a role field to AGENT.md,
read it there and keep this file only for overrides.

adaptive_grid_trader.notes: Grid trading, but the loop is directional: multi-timeframe analysis picks LONG/SHORT/TWO_SIDED and re-picks it as conditions move, so the grid is the execution shape rather than the job. Based on directional_trader over market_making_expert on grants too — its 9 tools are a strict subset of the directional base (which declares tools: [] and inherits all 24), while market making covers only 6 of them and adds manage_controllers and manage_bots, which this agent is not granted.

condor.notes: The chat assistant. Full surface, and the only domain whose name differs from its slug.

dca_accumulator.notes: Laddered spot accumulation via dca_executor — level spacing, per-level size, budget, and re-laddering after a move. Directional rather than market-making: it is one-sided accumulation with a long bias, explicitly not grids or two-sided quoting. Grants agree with the job, on the same reasoning as adaptive_grid_trader: its 9 tools are a strict subset of the directional base (which declares tools: [] and inherits all 24), while market making covers only 7 of them and misses trading_agent_journal_write and send_notification.

delta_neutral_funding_agent.notes: Beta-weighted pair market making. Same tools as the market-making base plus manage_routines.

directional_trader.notes: Declares tools: [] so it inherits all 24. Base for directional strategies.

market_making_expert.notes: Scoped to 8 tools. Base for connector-specific market-making strategies.

meteora_launch_lp.notes: Scoped to 7 tools and holds the only exclusive grant in the roster (manage_amm), so no other domain's evidence covers its core tool.

orca_lp_expert.notes: Concentrated-liquidity LP on Solana specialised to Orca CLMM pools and tokenized RWAs (SPCX, GME, SILV). Same job as the Solana LP base — pool attractiveness, range selection, IL and exit calls — pointed at one venue and one asset class, which is what makes it a strategy rather than a domain of its own. Note the grant runs the other way from the usual subset argument: it declares tools: [] and inherits all 24 while the base is scoped to 11, so the inherited assignment rests on evidence narrower than its surface.

smart_money_flow.notes: Directional perp trading on Derive. Declares tools: [] like its base.

solana_dex_lp_expert.notes: Scoped to 8 tools. Base for chain- or venue-specific LP strategies.

xrpl_market_maker.notes: Market making specialised to the XRPL CLOB connector.
